I need a channel beam with 70mm width, 40mm height, a length 450mm with a wall thickness of 5mm, which is open on the top side | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step plan (no execution yet)

1. Establish the basic solid  
   • Add one rectangular block that represents the full, “un-hollowed” beam:  
     – Length (X-direction): 450 mm  
     – Outer width (Y-direction): 70 mm  
     – Outer height (Z-direction): 40 mm  
     – Base point at the global origin (0, 0, 0)  
     – subtraction = False (because it forms the initial volume)

2. Hollow the inside while keeping 5 mm walls on the bottom and both sides, and leaving the top open  
   • Subtract a second rectangular block whose size is reduced by twice the wall thickness in Y, and by the wall thickness in Z:  
     – Length (X): 450 mm  (full length; the channel ends remain open)  
     – Inner width (Y): 70 mm – 2 × 5 mm = 60 mm (5 mm side walls left and right)  
     – Inner height (Z): 40 mm – 5 mm = 35 mm (5 mm bottom wall left; block reaches the outer top, so the top is removed)  
     – Its base point must be shifted inward by the wall thickness in Y and Z: (x=0, y=5, z=5)  
     – subtraction = True (to cut this volume out)

3. No further cuts are necessary because the second block already reaches the full 40 mm height, eliminating the top wall entirely and leaving the requested open channel.

Once you confirm, I will translate these two steps into the required block-function call with the correct array parameters.
